blocks.x: Event-log truth exposes the rework loops that every automation program quietly funds.
Process mining is the cheapest AI you will buy. Variant analysis routinely finds 10-30 rework loops per major process.
Task mining quantifies swivel-chair waste that surveys miss.
Conformance monitoring keeps target-state design honest after go-live.
Where this goes wrong in practice

Where it breaks in practice: autonomy granted faster than governance — agents shipped with policies nobody wrote down and telemetry nobody reads, until the incident review becomes the real policy meeting.
The serious opposition goes: the policy-first thesis can ossify into approvals that cost more than the work. Autonomy tiers need revisiting on a cadence, not once at launch.
The practice, as we run it

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: orchestration is the discipline — dozens of small automations running as one auditable workforce, with escalations designed rather than improvised. Every program in the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
A value assessment prices the delta in your estate before anything is signed: process mining is the cheapest AI you will buy, measured against your baseline, in two weeks.
